name: World-space HUD
oneLiner: HUD pieces that live in the world and follow the camera: a ring under every unit's feet with an HP arc whose pale loss segment drains after a hit, name plates with level and HP above heads that step up or sideways (with a leader line) so they never overlap each other, the game's HUD rects or the view edge, a marker with the distance in metres above the current goal, and arrows on the screen edge that point exactly at off-screen targets, sliding inward along the same bearing past HUD boxes. Crisp whole pixels with a built-in bitmap font on native pixel canvases, smooth vector drawing on HD canvases.
fits: tactics and real-time strategy maps (selection rings, unit plates)
twin-stick and arena games with tracked targets
notFor: side-view platformers (rings and plates read best seen from above; plates alone can work)
single-screen menus and card games (nothing in a world)
first-person 3D (needs a projected toScreen; not covered by the checks)

needs: units in world px with the feet point, footprint radius, sprite height, team, name, HP
the current goal (and any tracked target) in world px
the camera's world rect and the screen rect of the play view
the HUD rects to keep clear (bars, quest text, windows while open)
a fixed update step (also on the ?t= replay); a ground pass between floor and sprites
provides: drawn rings with HP arcs and loss drain, name plates, goal marker with distance, edge arrows with distance
rects() of every plate, arrow and marker (UI rects for other overlays)
lastDrawn(): where each ring, plate, arrow and marker is drawn, and what was hidden and why

params.label: Name plates (auto = party, targets, just-hit enemies)

assets: module/world-hud.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_WorldHud): rings with HP arc and loss drain, plate layout solver, goal marker, edge arrows with the bearing recomputed after sliding, crisp and smooth drawing, a built-in 5-row bitmap font and 5x5 badge icons
no image, font or audio files
